summary: [spec fidelity] An option given with no value at all reports `received: ""`, as if the caller had sent an empty string. `canon finding add --change --json`, `canon status --repo --json`, `canon query --kind --json` all print `message: a value is required for '--change <CHANGE_ID>' but none was supplied` with `received: ""`; only `--change ""` or `--change=` is an empty value the caller sent (those are right). Brief F4: `received: ""` for an empty value the caller sent; no `received` for a value never sent ("값 없이 부르면 received가 없다"). Cause: usage_parts takes `string(ContextKind::InvalidValue)`, which clap sets to "" in the missing-value error; 0.33 dropped every empty `received`, which hid it. The scenario-08 test only covers the option left out entirely, so the gap is unproven. Proposed fix: keep `received` only when the argv held the value (e.g. ErrorKind::InvalidValue with a non-missing value, or check the raw args for `--change=` / an empty following word); add `finding add --change` (no value) to the test. Blast radius: every option in the tree, text and JSON.
